newsitem.title: USA: US cash crudes consolidate, sour grades stay firm.
newsitem.headline: US cash crudes consolidate, sour grades stay firm.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices retreated slightly on Wednesday morning in a consolidative move tied to softer NYMEX futures prices.
August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was nearly five cents lower at $19.60-70 a barrel, with the August/September spread at -12 cents.
Cash dealers said bold gains in sour grade prices posted on Tuesday held through the early stages Wednesday. West Texas Sour/Midland was pegged around a $1.10 discount to the benchmark, traders said.

Sour barrels have gained strength on Colombian force majeure declarations for Cano Limon shipments. The 300,000 barrel per day capacity Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline was dynamited twice last week by Colombian National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas, leaving crude production shut-in.
Other grades saw Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sell at a 23 cents premium to the August marker, steady from late talk on Tuesday.

Midland/WTI sold at 21 cents under WTI/Cushing, again steady from previous trades. Other numbers in the Gulf had Eugene Island talked at $1.35-25 under the marker, with Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire 35-25 cents cheaper.
WTI/Cushing Postings Plus was at $1.86-91, within ranges seen yesterday.
